headline: Donbas-for-NATO Question Still Lacks Settlement Terms
deck: Zelensky says the Americans asked whether Ukraine would leave parts of Donbas for NATO membership; no reciprocal terms are public.
body: Volodymyr Zelensky said the Americans had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas if it joined NATO. He said it was the first time they had raised that question. [E1]
The Guardian reported that the question concerned parts of the eastern Donbas region that Russia does not control, putting Ukrainian-held territory inside the reported question. [E3]
Zelensky said he could not decide whether to accept the idea on his own and that the discussions still lacked specifics. [E2]
He also said the discussion had put NATO back on Ukraine’s agenda after Ukraine received defence support and developed its armed forces. [E4]

The sequence follows the Abu Dhabi talks, which produced the prisoner-exchange coverage this paper published on 12 and 13 November: “Russia and Ukraine Agree to Prisoner Exchange” and “POW Terms Leave Abu Dhabi Short of a Peace Settlement.” In the latter, Jared Kushner, the U.S. presidential envoy, said Russia and Ukraine had agreed final terms for a prisoner-of-war exchange. [E5]

**The desk's reading.** The stronger reading is that the reported question establishes a negotiating threshold: it identifies territory, NATO membership and Ukraine’s decision process as connected conditions, but leaves the reciprocal terms unspecified. The best competing reading is that putting the question directly shows a settlement framework is already taking shape. A framework would need a stated exchange that both sides can assess, rather than a question described by one participant.

**The next test.** At the next public account of the talks, either the United States, Russia or Ukraine should put a concrete reciprocal term on the record: what territorial step is sought, what security or membership commitment accompanies it, and who must accept it. Matching terms acknowledged by the relevant sides would support the settlement-framework reading; continued accounts of questions without those terms would support the threshold reading.
